title: The Cipher of the Fens
premise: Retired detective Coral Sandoval, who quietly solved three 'accidental' deaths from her failing fen-side bookshop, is paid a suspiciously large retainer by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder will not happen — the murder of his sister, a police archivist who has gone missing. As Coral investigates, she realizes the killer is someone with intimate access to the original case files of her three solved deaths: a ghost from her past who has been erasing witnesses one by one. The missing archivist, it turns out, staged her own disappearance to bait the killer into the open, and Coral must choose between protecting her found family at the bookshop and walking into the trap herself. In the climax on the frozen fens, Coral trades her evidence for the archivist's life, outwits the killer using a cipher hidden in the very case file he memorized, and finally lets go of the guilt over the death she failed to prevent years ago.
about_author: Gideon Coldharbour is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent twenty years transcribing testimony in coastal towns before turning to crime fiction. He lives near tidal marshes, where he claims every fog conceals at least one unsolved thing.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A rain-soaked stranger named Elias Vane pays six months' rent upfront to prove his sister Maren hasn't been murdered — only that she's missing. Coral, whose bookshop is weeks from closing, takes the money despite the wrongness of it. Beat: reluctant hope tangled with unease.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, Revisited
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. She reviews her three quietly solved cases — a drowning, a fall, a fire — all ruled accidents, all hers to close off the record. Each victim had one thing in common: contact with the county archive. Beat: cold recognition that a pattern was always there.

chapters.title: The Empty Flat
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with a brief interlude from her shop assistant Dev. Maren's flat is staged too neatly: kettle warm, shoes paired, a library card for the police archive left deliberately visible. Someone wanted the room read a certain way. Beat: creeping certainty that Maren left a message.

chapters.title: Dev Knows Too Much
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Dev admits he recognized Maren as a regular customer and that she once asked him about Coral's old cases. Coral feels betrayed, then sees Dev's fear and folds him into the investigation — the first member of her found family conscripted. Beat: friction becoming loyalty.

chapters.title: The Cipher in the Margins
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In Maren's borrowed library books, Coral finds pencil marks — a numeric cipher keyed to archival call numbers. Deciphered, the first fragment reads: HE READS THE FILES BEFORE YOU DO. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: An Old Colleague's Warning
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral visits DI Harrow, her former partner, who warns her off and lets slip that a fourth 'accident' is being processed — a boating death matching her pattern exactly. He also mentions a records clerk transferred out under strange circumstances years ago. Beat: the past leaning on the present.

chapters.title: The Man Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Elias Vane cannot be found; his hotel room holds only a burner phone and a photograph of Coral taken outside her shop. She realizes she wasn't hired — she was summoned. Beat: vertigo, the hunter realizing she is prey.

chapters.title: What the Water Gave Back
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. At the boating accident site she finds the fourth victim wore Maren's coat. Either Maren is dead, or the killer is staging her death early. A witness sketch of a man at the dock matches no one — except a face from Coral's earliest case. Beat: grief and denial wrestling.

chapters.title: The Bookshop Siege of Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs — Dev, neighbor Mrs. Okonkwo, teenage regular Priya. The found family fortifies the shop without being asked, keeping it open as an anchor while Coral works. Beat: warmth as resistance against encroaching fear.

chapters.title: The Clerk Who Vanished
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Digging into the transferred clerk, Coral finds Thomas Reeve: a man obsessed with case integrity, humiliated when her first solved death made his filing look negligent. He didn't just read the files — he believed he owned them. Beat: the antagonist taking human shape.

chapters.title: Maren Is Alive
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (first appearance). Hidden in a fenland bothy, Maren reveals she staged her disappearance after finding Reeve's annotations inside sealed files — proof he'd been present at all four deaths. She used Elias Vane, a frightened client, unknowingly, to hire the one detective Reeve respects. Beat: guilt braided with resolve.

chapters.title: The Trap She Set for Herself
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren's plan required Coral to follow the cipher to a dead-drop; instead Reeve intercepted it, and now he knows where Maren hides. She must move or lose the advantage. Beat: the trap turning on its architect.

chapters.title: Harrow's Choice
chapters.summary: Harrow's POV. Harrow discovers Reeve's access logs but hesitates to report — exposing Reeve means exposing how long the force ignored Coral's warnings. Duty versus conscience; he burns nothing but tells Coral everything. Beat: an ally bought with shame.

chapters.title: Cipher Complete
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The full decoded message reveals Maren copied Reeve's annotated files and hid them — but the hiding place is described only in terms Coral recognizes: the drowned church on the fens, site of her first case, site of her greatest failure. Beat: the past demanding payment.

chapters.title: What Coral Failed to Prevent
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, flashback-woven. The story of the death she couldn't stop — her informant, drowned within sight of the drowned church — and how Reeve filed it as an accident while she knew better. Her retirement, her shop, her silence: all built on that night. Beat: confession to herself.

chapters.title: The Ransom Note
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Reeve contacts her directly: bring the copied files to the church or Maren dies tonight. He addresses her by her old rank. He wants not the papers but her acknowledgment that his filings were right and hers were trespass. Beat: the case becoming personal theology.

chapters.title: Preparing the Ground
chapters.summary: Dev, Priya, and Mrs. Okonkwo's POVs. While Coral plans, the family prepares without instruction — Dev copies the files, Priya maps the fen paths, Mrs. Okonkwo feeds everyone. Love expressed as logistics. Beat: tenderness under pressure.

chapters.title: The Drowned Church
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On the ice-glazed fens at dusk, Coral makes the exchange. Reeve produces Maren, bound, and demands Coral recant her verdicts aloud. She begins to — then recites, instead, the errors in his own filings, proving he falsified records to protect his theory. Beat: the pivot from surrender to attack.

chapters.title: Thin Ice
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral/Maren POV. Reeve snaps; the chase crosses cracking ice toward the submerged nave. Maren frees herself using the trick hidden in her own cipher. Reeve, pursuing the files rather than escape, breaks through into the flooded crypt. Beat: obsession collecting its debt.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral goes in after him — not to save him, but because she refused to let another person drown unrecorded. She pulls him half-living onto the ice; he survives, broken, muttering corrections to his own files. Beat: mercy chosen against instinct.

chapters.title: Case Closed, Quietly
chapters.summary: Harrow's POV. Officialdom absorbs the truth: four murders, one clerk, one retired detective. Harrow offers Coral reinstatement and a commendation; she declines both but accepts his apology. Maren's statement clears Elias Vane, who was only ever a frightened brother. Beat: vindication without appetite.

chapters.title: Open Sign
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Spring comes to the fens. The bookshop thrives modestly; Maren works part-time shelving true crime alphabetized wrong on purpose; Dev, Priya, and Mrs. Okonkwo argue over the till. Coral keeps the cipher framed above the door — a reminder that memory, like love, is a duty you choose. Beat: peace earned, not given.
